card.line: Ephesus was a major city of the province of Asia, home to the temple of Artemis, where Paul taught for about two years and the gospel spread widely.

moments.title: Paul's short first visit
moments.text: Paul stopped at Ephesus and reasoned with the Jews in the synagogue. When they asked him to stay longer, he declined, promising to return if God was willing.

moments.title: Apollos is taught more fully
moments.text: Apollos, a skilled speaker who knew the Scriptures, came to Ephesus and spoke boldly. Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more accurately.

moments.title: The Holy Spirit comes on disciples
moments.text: Paul found about twelve disciples who knew only John's baptism. They were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them.

moments.title: The riot over Artemis
moments.text: Demetrius the silversmith stirred up the craftsmen, who feared Paul's teaching would hurt their business and the temple of Artemis. The crowd rushed into the theatre shouting until the city clerk quieted them.

moments.title: Paul sends for the elders
moments.text: Paul decided to sail past Ephesus because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem. From nearby Miletus he sent for the elders of the Ephesian church, and they came to him.
